text.p: Romania's parliament on Tuesday elected a Supreme Court judge as the country's first ombudsman.
Paul Mitroi, 60, a judge at the court's economic section since the December 1989 anti-communist revolution, won 73 votes in the 143-member Senate.
Mitroi served last year as head of the election board overseeing general elections which brought centrists to power after seven years of rule by former communists.
Under Romania's 1991 Constitution, the ombudsman is elected for a four-year term to defend individual rights, fight abuses of authority, violations of the law and tackle bureaucracy.
He has no power to become involved in cases before the courts, but may intervene with local authorities if he feels an individual's rights have been infringed and also demand changes in legislation.

Most east European countries, including Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary have had an ombudsman in place for several years. Ukraine has a provision for an ombudsman in its constitution but has so far failed to appoint one. REUTER
